messages:
nate: Heads-up — canary with the new dynamic tensor-pool packing landed, but we're seeing a 95p latency regression at seq_len 256.

sarah: Ugh. That was supposed to save memory and reduce stalls, right?

nate: It does reduce VRAM by ~18% (see profiler extract below) but tail latency jumped. Suspect logits buffer alignment + kernel selector fallback.

aj: Can you paste the profiler snippet / kernel selection log?

nate: Sure, here's the short trace from the canary run:
```
[profiler] route=/generate-chat seq=256 batch=8
kernel_select: fast_matmul_v1 chosen=false reason="stride_mismatch"
memcpy: logits_packed->scratchpad 1.18ms (cudaMemcpyAsync)
kernel: generic_matmul 3.92ms
kv_cache_update memcpy 0.42ms
total_step 8.45ms   baseline (no-packing) 6.03ms
mem_saved 18.2% of model workspace
```
Also saw more frequent fallback to generic attention kernels when packed layout present.

jin: Did you reproduce with the batcher forced to static (no dynamic packing)?

nate: Yes — with packing disabled tails return to baseline. So packing reduces memory but sometimes forces a slower code path.

kevin: Likely root cause: kernel selector uses leading-dimension/stride heuristics. Packed logits change the stride/ld, selector prefers a generic kernel that needs an extra copy or different launch params.

sarah: Any evidence of additional memcpy happening in scratchpad handling vs normal flow?

nate: Profiler shows explicit memcpy from packed logits to an aligned scratchpad before kernel launch. That memcpy is the ~1.18ms hit per step in the table above.

todd: Two directions: (A) teach kernel selector about packed layout so it can pick an accelerated kernel that accepts the stride OR (B) change packing policy so it's not used for latency-sensitive routes.

aj: Another option: only enable packing when batch_size >= N or seq-length variance is low. Packing helps throughput but hurts skewed/beam cases.

sarah: What's the net cost/benefit in prod? How many routes need the memory saving vs how many are latency sensitive?

nate: Memory saved allows us to host models with ~2x context in some fleets. But for customer-facing chat routes the 95p regression is unacceptable.

dev-bot: Canary alert: route=/generate-chat 95p latency increased 40% vs baseline (since 2026-03-18T14:02Z).

kevin: Also note: KV cache interaction is tricky — packing can change offsets expected by KV update kernels. If we pack activations but leave KV cache contiguous, we end up extra mapping/memcpy.

jin: Could we keep KV cache layout untouched and only pack transient logits/activation scratchpads? That reduces KV headaches.

nate: We tried that: it helps but not fully. The major extra memcpy is between packed logits and an aligned matmul scratchpad required by the current matmul kernel.

aj: A mitigation to test: async cudaMemcpyAsync + overlapped streams to hide the copy behind other work. May help if we can overlap KV updates or other ops.

todd: I'll schedule two canaries:
  - canary A: packing threshold = batch>=16 (more conservative)
  - canary B: packing enabled + kernel-selector-hint to prefer pack-aware kernels (if available)

qa-bot: Test matrix added to nightly perf:
  - batches: [1,4,8,16]
  - seqs: [64,128,256]
  - kv_cache_hit: [0,50,100]
  - beam_search: [1,4]

nate: Also observed that beam search multiplies misalignment issues — beams with varying lengths cause packing to produce irregular strides.

kevin: Short-term fix: revert dynamic packing on routes annotated latency:SLO in runtime routing. Long-term: extend kernel libs to accept strided inputs or add a pack-aware matmul.

sarah: Can we add a runtime flag per-route so we don't have to toggle globally?

todd: Yes, we can. I'll add a per-route config switch and a rollout plan.

nate: PR created: https://git/repo/pull/3141 — "Gate dynamic-logits-packing per-route + kernel selector trace flag". Added profiler traces and an opt-in for pack-aware kernels.

aj: Reviewing the PR now. Quick question in the PR: do we surface a `will_copy` boolean in the kernel trace so we can measure how often packing causes copies?

nate: I added `kernel_trace.will_copy=true/false` to the tracer in the PR.

kevin: For the kernel team: we should prioritize adding a pack-friendly matmul kernel. It may be slightly more codegen work but avoids the memcpy.

sarah: Operational decision (proposal): enable packing for throughput routes (batching-heavy) and disable for latency routes. Add telemetry to re-evaluate monthly.

todd: I'll implement the per-route gating + canary. Rollout policy: 10% -> 30% -> 60% with 95p rollback threshold = baseline * 1.2.

dev-bot: Rollout started: 10% of nodes updated, 0 errors so far. Monitoring 95p every minute.

nate: I'll drop the full perf logs here: /var/tmp/perf/2276543210.log and attach a short flamegraph in the PR.

aj: Thanks — will leave comments on the PR. :thumbsup: \n
todd: Closing loop: canary updated, QA matrix running. If 95p > baseline*1.2 at any stage we auto-rollback.

dev-bot: Canary progress: 30% nodes updated, observed 12% median latency change, 95p trending +18% (watching).
